thread_title: S. psittacina var. okefenokeensis Santa Rosa Co, FL
breadcrumb: S. psittacina var. okefenokeensis Santa Rosa Co, FL

posts.body_html:
Parrot pitcher plants remind me of S. leucophylla a bit: there's a whole lot of phenotypic variation from one year to the next. Take this S. psittacina var. okefenokeensis from Santa Rosa Co, FL as an example: last year, it produced very small plants, but the "heads" were very large had had rather short, stubby and thin petioles. This year, the heads are still sorta roundish (they don't look as amazing as last year's traps) but now the petioles are winged and much longer. Normally, we don't get the best traps here in northern California until early to late fall, so fingers crossed this is just the beginning.

These plants aren't yet giant, but they're not small either. Photos taken 8/14/15:

posts.body_html: Cleaned them all up and repotted these fatties! They're pretty darn giant right now, but they can get bigger. You can sorta tell how big the traps are by comparing them to the size of my hands (medium sized hands BTW LOL). To recap, I think these parrot pitcher plants look best during the dormancy period! Photos 3/13/18. as an aside, notice all those blurry divisions in the background: MW has been slaving over that for the past few months to make some of the harder to get plants more available:

posts.body_html:
Established divisions of my best Santa Rosa Co, FL just starting to take off! This is what ends up on your doorstep, these are actual plants offered! these are all the same clone. Pics taken 8/9/19:






The big mother plant hasn't done much this year, but they typically put on their best growth in the fall, hopefully I'll have some monster traps to share with ye all. Hopefully to be continued soon!
